title: Environment
description: Words for Task 2 essays and Speaking Part 3 on climate change, pollution, conservation and natural resources.

words.definition: to make something harmful less severe
words.example: Planting trees along busy roads can help mitigate the effects of air pollution.

words.definition: gases or other substances released into the air
words.example: Transport is responsible for a large share of carbon emissions in most cities.

words.definition: coming from a source that is not used up, such as wind or sunlight
words.example: Indonesia has enormous potential for renewable energy, particularly geothermal power.

words.definition: the cutting down of forests over a large area
words.example: Deforestation for palm oil plantations has destroyed the habitat of many endangered species.

words.definition: the variety of plants and animals living in a particular area
words.example: Coral reefs are among the richest areas of biodiversity on the planet.

words.definition: the natural home of an animal or plant
words.example: As cities expand, many birds are losing their natural habitat.

words.definition: at serious risk of no longer existing
words.example: The Sumatran tiger is one of the most endangered big cats in the world.

words.definition: the protection of nature, wildlife and natural resources
words.example: Tourism can fund conservation projects if it is carefully managed.

words.definition: able to continue for a long time without damaging the environment
words.example: Governments should encourage more sustainable forms of farming.

words.definition: fuels such as coal, oil and gas formed from ancient plants and animals
words.example: Reducing our dependence on fossil fuels is essential if we want to slow global warming.

words.definition: the amount of carbon dioxide produced by a person's or organisation's activities
words.example: Flying less is one of the most effective ways to reduce your carbon footprint.

words.definition: to make something dirty or harmful by adding a dangerous substance
words.example: Waste from the factory had contaminated the river for several kilometres.

words.definition: a reduction in the amount of something until little is left
words.example: Overfishing has led to the severe depletion of fish stocks in the region.

words.definition: all the living things in an area and the way they affect each other and their environment
words.example: Introducing a foreign species can upset the balance of an entire ecosystem.

words.definition: the process of something becoming worse in quality
words.example: Intensive farming has caused serious soil degradation in some parts of the country.

words.definition: a long period with little or no rain
words.example: Prolonged droughts are making it harder for farmers to grow rice.

words.definition: a substance that makes air, water or soil dirty or harmful
words.example: Vehicle exhaust contains several pollutants that are harmful to human health.

words.definition: a place where large amounts of rubbish are buried
words.example: Most plastic packaging still ends up in landfill rather than being recycled.

words.definition: intended to be used once and then thrown away
words.example: Several cities have banned disposable plastic bags in supermarkets.

words.definition: impossible to change back to a previous condition
words.example: Scientists warn that some damage to the polar ice sheets may already be irreversible.

words.definition: to balance the effect of something with an opposite effect
words.example: Some airlines let passengers offset their emissions by paying for tree planting.

words.definition: rain, snow or hail that falls to the ground
words.example: The graph shows average monthly precipitation in three Asian cities.

words.definition: the situation in which a species no longer exists
words.example: Without stronger protection, the orangutan could be driven to extinction.

words.definition: the warming of the Earth caused by gases that trap heat in the atmosphere
words.example: Burning coal intensifies the greenhouse effect by releasing carbon dioxide.

words.definition: to control or limit something, especially something harmful
words.example: Stricter regulations are needed to curb industrial pollution.

words.definition: not harmful to the environment
words.example: Consumers are increasingly willing to pay more for eco-friendly products.

words.definition: a sudden flood caused by heavy rain in a short time
words.example: Poor drainage makes many urban areas vulnerable to flash floods during the rainy season.

words.definition: to keep something in its original state or protect it from harm
words.example: National parks were created to preserve areas of outstanding natural beauty.

words.definition: the use of more resources than is necessary or sustainable
words.example: Overconsumption in wealthy countries places a heavy burden on the planet's resources.

words.definition: an increase in the average height of the oceans
words.example: Coastal cities such as Jakarta are particularly vulnerable to sea-level rise.
